8.description: The Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Advisory Committee will draft its 2026 work plan, outlining future initiatives on policy, membership, and community engagement for Council review.

chips.text: Councillor noted prescriptive land acknowledgements cause people to tune out.
No one connected with Environmental Advisory Committee on social media strategy.
Committee seeks second 2SLGBTQIA+ member to represent transgender and non-binary communities.

10.description: Saskatoon City Council received the current Statement of Expenditures for 2025, noting no significant changes to the budget at this time.

chips.text: The process for submitting follow-up reports for events is unclear.

12.description: Saskatoon temporarily suspended the Living in Harmony Awards due to limited staff capacity and low participation from overwhelmed teachers, as reported by school boards.

chips.text: Only a few enthusiastic teachers repeatedly applied for the awards.

20.description: The Living in Harmony Awards program will be re-evaluated to boost participation and community engagement. The committee aims to simplify expectations, modernize submissions, and rebuild school board relationships.

chips.text: Submissions for the awards program have significantly declined in recent years.
The awards program is designed for youth and children under 18.
Administrative work is needed before the subcommittee can effectively workshop new strategies.
The committee questioned if the program should be rebranded for greater relevance.

21.description: The city's Diversity and Inclusion Consultant highlighted a lack of professional development for Indigenous and racialized frontline workers, and announced upcoming Asian Heritage Month events and a March 27 Round Dance.

chips.text: IRCC funding cuts are eliminating upper-level English language classes and jobs.
Asylum-seeking refugees are receiving support from grassroots organizations.
Cuts to English language classes (levels 5+) hinder immigrants' post-secondary access.
City hopes to offer professional development training for frontline workers, pending funding.

15.description: City advisory committees must adhere to their budgets, with changes over $2,000 requiring approval. A review of all committee mandates and structures is also underway.

chips.text: Advisory committee members can engage fully in the upcoming mandate review process.
Clerk's office will engage each committee individually on their mandate and structure.
